papers.title: Unraveling the pathogenic mechanisms of osteoarthritis and obesity: An integration of GWAS, cellular specificity, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically elucidate the shared and specific genetic basis of osteoarthritis (OA) and obesity by integrating large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, cross-tissue quantitative trait loci (QTLs), and single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data.
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, QTL, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to systematically identify shared and distinct genetic mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis and obesity. It aims to uncover cell-type-specific and spatially resolved pathways that link these two conditions, potentially revealing novel therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A multi-omics integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies and validates a 16-gene epithelial-mesenchymal transition prognostic signature in tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes, highlighting the critical need for dependable prognostic indicators. The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a fundamental biological process driving cancer progression. This study aimed to develop and independently validate an EMT-associated gene expression signature for predicting prognosis in TSCC through a multi-omics strategy.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated a 16-gene prognostic signature based on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) gene expression for tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC), using a multi-omics approach that integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics. The signature independently predicts patient outcomes, offering a potentially reliable clinical tool for risk stratification in TSCC.

papers.title: AI-Guided Long Non-Coding RNA Target Discovery for Precision Medicine: Integrating GWAS, Multi-Omics, Experimental Validation, and RNA Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Precision medicine requires translation of genetic and molecular variation into clinically actionable therapeutic targets. However, many disease-associated signals identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) reside in non-coding regulatory regions, making biological interpretation and therapeutic prioritization difficult. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules with growing relevance to disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and RNA-based therapeutics. This review presents a translational framework for AI-guided lncRNA t
papers.summary: This review outlines a framework for using AI to identify long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as therapeutic targets, integrating GWAS data, multi-omics, experimental validation, and RNA therapeutics for precision medicine. It addresses the challenge of interpreting non-coding disease-associated variants and highlights the potential of lncRNAs in biomarker discovery and patient stratification.

papers.title: GRAIL-heart: A graph attention network for inferring ligand-receptor interactions in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication through ligand-receptor (L-R) interactions orchestrates cardiac development, homeostasis, and disease progression, yet existing computational methods cannot infer directional signalling networks or distinguish causal from correlational interactions in spatial transcriptomics data. We present GRAIL-Heart, a graph-attention-based framework that integrates spatial tissue topology with multi-task learning to predict context-dependent L-R interactions, reconstruct gene expression, and infer causal signalling pathways. Validated on 42,654 cells across six cardiac regions from
papers.summary: GRAIL-heart is a new graph attention network that infers ligand-receptor interactions from spatial transcriptomics data, integrating spatial topology with multi-task learning to predict directional signaling and distinguish causal from correlational interactions. Validated on cardiac tissue, it reconstructs gene expression and infers causal signaling pathways, offering a more nuanced tool for studying cell-cell communication.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals 4-HNE-related stromal remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: 4-HNE is a lipid peroxidation product involved in oxidative stress, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and tumor progression. This study aimed to characterize the cellular distribution, prognostic relevance, and functional roles of 4-HNE-related molecular features in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular distribution and functional roles of 4-HNE, a lipid peroxidation product, in lung adenocarcinoma. The findings reveal 4-HNE-related stromal remodeling and its association with prognosis, providing new insights into oxidative stress in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Pan-tumor spatial transcriptomics reveals conserved properties of tumor organization.
papers.abstract: Tumor microenvironments (TMEs) are compositionally and functionally heterogeneous, making it challenging to discover organizing structural principles. Through a study of 262 solid tumors profiled by spatial transcriptomics, we identify a conserved architecture where TMEs are partitioned into discrete, hierarchically organized multicellular sub-regions, which we term "spatial groups" (SGs). As indicated by orthogonal spatial measurements and expert pathologist review, SGs associate with recognizable biological domains spanning global tissue context to local cellular neighborhoods. Comparing tum
papers.summary: This study analyzes spatial transcriptomics data from 262 solid tumors and identifies a conserved organizational principle: tumor microenvironments are partitioned into discrete, hierarchically organized multicellular sub-regions termed 'spatial groups' (SGs). These SGs correspond to recognizable biological domains, validated by orthogonal spatial measurements and expert pathologist review, revealing a common architectural framework across diverse tumor types.

papers.title: Lactylation-related immune-metabolic dysregulation defines prognostic and therapeutic stratification in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lactylation links lactate metabolism with inflammatory signaling and immune regulation in tumors. However, its cellular distribution and translational value in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates lactylation-related immune-metabolic dysregulation in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), revealing that lactylation patterns are associated with distinct immune and metabolic profiles that can stratify patients by prognosis and therapeutic response. The findings suggest that lactylation-related gene signatures could serve as prognostic biomarkers and guide treatment decisions in LUAD.

papers.title: Maladaptive immune-fibrotic axis drives impaired long bone regeneration under mechanical instability.
papers.abstract: Delayed and nonhealing fractures, affecting 5 to 10% of cases, are associated with prolonged disability and diminished quality of life. Although acute inflammation is required to initiate repair, persistent mechanical instability can sustain maladaptive immune and fibrotic responses that impede regeneration. Existing animal models do not adequately recapitulate mechanical instability, the principal driver of hypertrophic nonunion in clinical settings, thereby limiting translational relevance. We developed a murine model of delayed fracture healing using tunable intramedullary fixation to impos
papers.summary: This study introduces a new mouse model of delayed fracture healing that mimics mechanical instability, a key driver of nonunion in patients. Using this model, the authors identify a maladaptive immune-fibrotic axis that impairs long bone regeneration, providing a more clinically relevant platform for studying and treating nonhealing fractures.

papers.title: Current Advances in Spatial Pathology of Nasal Polyps: Challenges, Opportunities for Artificial Intelligence, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is characterized by inflammatory heterogeneity, epithelial hyperplasia, and tissue remodeling, with spatial pathology critical for deciphering pathological mechanisms and guiding clinical practice. Conventional histopathological techniques rely on subjective visual evaluation, limited by inadequate spatial resolution of molecular markers and imprecise quantitative analysis. Recent advances show that spatial transcriptomics reveals nasal polyps (NP) inflammatory heterogeneity; deep learning enables automated inflammatory subset identification an
papers.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This review discusses recent advances in spatial pathology of nasal polyps, highlighting how spatial transcriptomics and deep learning can overcome limitations of conventional histopathology by revealing inflammatory heterogeneity and enabling automated analysis. It emphasizes the potential of these technologies to improve understanding of disease mechanisms and guide clinical practice, while also addressing challenges and future directions for artificial intelligence in this field.

papers.title: Spatially-resolved pharmaco-ecology of immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for mechanism-matched combination therapies.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have reshaped the treatment landscape of lung adenocarcinoma, but primary, adaptive and acquired resistance are still the main clinical obstacles. This review integrates LUAD-specific evidence with broader NSCLC single-cell and spatial-omics studies, emphasizing lung adenocarcinoma where subtype-specific data are available. We discuss how therapeutic stress can select or induce malignant epithelial states that manifest as impaired antigen presentation, altered interferon signaling, partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition, stress tolerance, and hypoxia-related met
papers.summary: This review synthesizes single-cell and spatial transcriptomics evidence to explain how therapeutic stress from immune checkpoint inhibitors drives resistance in lung adenocarcinoma by selecting or inducing malignant epithelial states, including impaired antigen presentation, altered interferon signaling, partial EMT, and hypoxia-related programs. It proposes mechanism-matched combination therapies guided by spatially resolved pharmaco-ecology, offering a framework to overcome primary, adaptive, and acquired resistance.

papers.title: st2traj: deconvolution-informed trajectory inference for multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics enables study of developmental processes in native tissue context, but cell-state mixtures within spots and lack of direct spatial correspondence across sections complicate trajectory inference and biological interpretation.
papers.summary: This paper introduces st2traj, a computational method that integrates deconvolution with trajectory inference to analyze multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenges of cell-state mixtures within spatial spots and the lack of direct spatial correspondence across tissue sections, enabling more accurate developmental trajectory reconstruction and biological interpretation.

papers.title: DeepPathway: Predicting Pathway Expression from Histopathology Images.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies provide spatially resolved gene expression along with image data, allowing the integrative analysis of complex tissue microenvironment. Despite their potential, the widespread adoption of ST remains limited due to high costs, and methodological challenges in data acquisition. Thus, there have been recent efforts to develop deep learning methods for inferring spatial gene expression from much cheaper and easily available haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images. These methods demonstrate promising results in reconstructing transcriptomic landscapes within ti
papers.summary: DeepPathway is a deep learning method that predicts pathway-level expression from H&E histopathology images, offering a cost-effective alternative to spatial transcriptomics. It demonstrates promising results in reconstructing transcriptomic landscapes within tissues, potentially enabling broader studies of the tumor microenvironment without expensive ST assays.

papers.title: STcompare: comparative spatial transcriptomics data analysis of structurally matched tissues to characterize differentially spatially patterned genes.
papers.abstract: Comparative analysis of spatial transcriptomics (ST) data is needed to identify genes that spatially change in their expression patterns between conditions, such as in diseased versus healthy tissues. Existing methods generally fail to distinguish changes in spatial patterning by focusing only on changes in gene expression magnitude for methods adapted from non-spatial data or on changes in significance of spatial variability for methods focusing on spatially-resolved data.
papers.summary: STcompare is a new computational tool for comparative spatial transcriptomics that identifies genes with altered spatial expression patterns between conditions (e.g., diseased vs. healthy tissues) by analyzing structurally matched tissue sections. Unlike existing methods that focus only on expression magnitude or spatial variability significance, STcompare specifically detects changes in spatial patterning, addressing a key gap in the field.

papers.title: Protocol to characterize tumor microenvironment in a diffuse midline glioma mouse model using multi-omics approach on sequential sections.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) tumors form complex tumor-immune microenvironments with marked cellular heterogeneity. Here, we present a protocol to generate orthotopic DMG tumors in immunocompetent neonatal mice and to spatially characterize the tumor ecosystem using a multi-omics workflow on sequential brain sections. We detail procedures for brain freezing, cryosectioning, single-nuclei RNA sequencing, and Visium spatial transcriptomics. We then describe steps for cyclic immunofluorescence and integrative computational analysis to resolve cellular states and spatial organization. For complete
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes a multi-omics workflow to characterize the tumor microenvironment in a diffuse midline glioma (DMG) mouse model, combining single-nuclei RNA sequencing, Visium spatial transcriptomics, and cyclic immunofluorescence on sequential brain sections. It provides a detailed method for generating orthotopic DMG tumors in immunocompetent neonatal mice and integrating these data to resolve cellular states and spatial organization.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning to identify specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets and chronic inflammation as key drivers of poor outcomes in ovarian cancer, particularly in residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight potential therapeutic targets and biomarkers for this deadly malignancy.

papers.title: Tumor-Intrinsic DNA Damage Signaling Is Associated with MHC-I Expression and CD8 Cytotoxic T-Cell Engagement in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by marked immune microenvironment heterogeneity and variable chemotherapy response, yet the epithelial transcriptional programs governing cytotoxic immune activation remain poorly understood. We performed an exploratory, integrative analysis using single-cell RNA sequencing of 31,962 cells from eight TNBC patients operationally stratified into Good and Bad Prognosis groups based on pathological lymphoid infiltration, a discovery grouping subsequently validated against pathological complete response (pCR) in three independent bulk RNA-seq co
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of TNBC tumors to show that tumor-intrinsic DNA damage signaling is associated with higher MHC-I expression and greater CD8+ T-cell engagement, linking epithelial transcriptional programs to cytotoxic immune activation. The findings suggest that DNA damage response pathways may influence immune infiltration and chemotherapy response in TNBC.

papers.title: Circulating Homocysteine and Choroid Plexus Volume Across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: Cross-Sectional and Progression-Related Associations.
papers.abstract: Elevated plasma homocysteine (HCY) is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its relationship with structural brain changes across the AD continuum remains unclear. The choroid plexus (CP) regulates cerebrospinal fluid homeostasis and may interface with peripheral metabolic signals. Whether HCY relates to CP structural alterations and disease progression remains unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates the association between elevated plasma homocysteine and choroid plexus volume across the Alzheimer's disease continuum, finding that higher HCY levels are linked to CP structural changes and may relate to disease progression. The findings suggest that HCY could influence AD through CP-mediated mechanisms, offering a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication (CCC), organizing them into three groups based on their analytical frameworks. It highlights how spatial context improves CCC inference over single-cell RNA-seq alone and provides a structured guide to help researchers select appropriate methods for their biological questions.

papers.title: A Neuro-Immune Score Defines a Stromal-Neural and Immune-Segregated Microenvironment Associated with Poor Prognosis in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer progression and therapeutic response are determined not only by tumor-intrinsic programs but also by neural, stromal, and immune components of the tumor microenvironment. However, biologically interpretable transcriptomic scores that jointly capture neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation remain limited. We developed a neuro-immune score (NIS), defined as the neural/stromal module score minus the immune activation module score. NIS was constructed using the combined TCGA-COAD/READ colorectal cancer cohort and externally evaluated in independent Gene Expression Omnibus
papers.summary: This study introduces a neuro-immune score (NIS) that captures the balance between neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation in colorectal cancer. The NIS, defined as the neural/stromal module score minus the immune activation module score, was developed using TCGA data and validated in independent cohorts, and a high NIS was associated with poor prognosis, indicating a stromal-neural and immune-segregated microenvironment.

papers.title: Coordinated Expression of ADC Targets ERBB2, TACSTD2, and NECTIN4 in Bladder Cancer: A Multi-Scale Transcriptomic and Proteomic Landscape Analysis.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) targeting HER2 (encoded by ERBB2), Trop2 (TACSTD2), and Nectin-4 (NECTIN4) have demonstrated clinical activity in bladder cancer. However, the co-expression relationships among these three targets at both the transcriptomic and protein levels, and their spatial organization within the tumor microenvironment, remain incompletely characterized. To address this, we performed a multi-platform, multi-resolution analysis integrating ten bulk RNA-seq datasets (n = 1628 samples), six spatial transcriptomics datasets (10x Visium and Visium HD, n = 31 specimens), and mult
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive multi-scale analysis of the expression of three ADC targets (ERBB2, TACSTD2, NECTIN4) in bladder cancer, integrating bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and proteomic data. The findings reveal coordinated expression patterns and spatial organization of these targets within the tumor microenvironment, which could inform patient selection and combination strategies for ADC therapies.

papers.title: DSG2 Expression Marks a Stromal-Immune Organizational State in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immune exclusion in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) limits immunotherapy efficacy, yet the molecular determinants of stromal-immune organization remain incompletely characterized. The desmosomal cadherin DSG2 is highly expressed in squamous epithelium; its role in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) is unknown.
papers.summary: This study identifies DSG2 expression as a marker of a specific stromal-immune organizational state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), potentially influencing immune exclusion and immunotherapy response. The findings suggest DSG2 may play a role in shaping the tumor microenvironment, offering a new avenue for understanding and targeting immune resistance.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the naive-to-primed pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The screen reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3, which together orchestrate the transcriptional and epigenetic changes required for this transition.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Omics Technologies in Rice Abiotic Stress Biology: A Methodological Review.
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses-drought, salinity, extreme temperature, flooding, and heavy-metal toxicity-constrain rice (Oryza sativa L.) yield worldwide, and the cellular programmes underlying them are unevenly distributed across cell types that bulk-tissue assays average together. This review examines, from a methodological standpoint, what single-cell and spatial omics technologies can and cannot establish about rice abiotic stress biology. We first define the modality space: single-cell omics measures RNA, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, protein, or metabolite features at the resolution of in
papers.summary: This methodological review evaluates the current and potential applications of single-cell and spatial omics technologies in studying rice responses to abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, and temperature extremes. It highlights how these approaches can reveal cell-type-specific molecular programs that are masked by bulk tissue analyses, while also discussing their limitations and future directions.

papers.title: Spatial Immune Coding in Tumor-Draining Lymph Nodes: Functional Compartmentalization of Immune Activation and Immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are important immune organs linking primary tumors with systemic immune responses. They support tumor antigen presentation, T-cell priming, and effector immune responses, but under sustained tumor influence they can also be remodeled into microenvironments that promote immune escape and metastatic colonization. Conventional methods, including flow cytometry, bulk RNA sequencing, and routine immunohistochemistry, have advanced our understanding of TDLN immunity but cannot simultaneously preserve tissue architecture, cell identity, and spatial cell-cell relatio
papers.summary: This review discusses the functional compartmentalization of tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs), highlighting how they can support both immune activation and immunosuppression depending on spatial organization. It emphasizes the need for spatial omics technologies to capture the architecture and cell-cell interactions that conventional methods miss, offering a framework for understanding TDLN immunity and potential therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, identifying potential mediating roles of inflammatory proteins. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa and inflammatory pathways may influence CNS tumor risk, offering new insights into the gut-immune-brain axis.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence data in a tissue-specific context for Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility, addressing a gap in existing genomic analysis tools.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Sequencing Analysis Identifies an Aging-Related Gene Signature for Prognosis in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence exerts a complex influence on BRCA progression and TME remodeling. However, the specific roles of ASIGs in regulating the TME and determining patient outcomes remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-sequencing data from breast cancer patients to identify an aging-related gene signature (ASIG) that predicts prognosis. The authors show that this signature is associated with tumor microenvironment remodeling and patient outcomes, providing a potential prognostic biomarker.

papers.title: SPIDER: spatially integrated denoising via embedding regularization with single cell supervision.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies profile gene expression while preserving tissue architecture, enabling the study of spatial cellular organization and microenvironmental interactions. However, raw ST data are heavily affected by technical noise, sparsity, and dropout events, which obscure true biological signals and hinder downstream analyses. While recent denoising methods incorporate spatial neighborhood information, they lack explicit supervision due to missing cell-type annotations in ST data. To address this challenge, we introduce SPIDER, a semi-supervised framework that leverag
papers.summary: SPIDER is a new semi-supervised framework for denoising spatial transcriptomics data. It integrates spatial neighborhood information with single-cell RNA-seq data to provide explicit supervision, effectively reducing technical noise and dropout while preserving tissue architecture. This improves downstream analyses by recovering clearer biological signals.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method that improves cell type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating transcriptional regulatory network information through iterative heterogeneous graph learning. It outperforms existing methods by more fully exploiting regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, leading to more accurate cell type identification.

papers.title: Multiscale learning of gene network-driven phenotypic dynamics of single cells.
papers.abstract: Understanding how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) dynamically orchestrate cell fate emergence remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present GRNvelo, a computational framework that reconstructs multiscale cell fate dynamics by integrating GRNs with phenotypic dynamics from temporal single-cell RNA-seq data. GRNvelo establishes a biologically interpretable and mathematically rigorous multiscale model that couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with nonlocal cell growth-mediated population dynamics. To operationalize this model, GRNvelo devises a two-phase cooperative optimization algorithm
papers.summary: GRNvelo is a new computational framework that integrates gene regulatory networks with temporal single-cell RNA-seq data to reconstruct multiscale cell fate dynamics. It couples GRN-driven single-cell velocity with population-level growth dynamics using a two-phase optimization algorithm, providing a biologically interpretable model of how gene networks orchestrate cell fate emergence.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper reports a rapid, ligand-based protocol for differentiating human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a new in vitro model for studying human ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. Single-cell RNA-sequencing was used to characterize the differentiated cells, confirming expression of developmental lineage markers and steroidogenic pathway genes.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Analyses Link Arachidonic Acid Metabolic Reprogramming to Proneural-to-Mesenchymal State Transition in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glioblastoma (GBM) is widely recognised as a highly aggressive form of malignant tumour arising within the central nervous system. The proneural-to-mesenchymal (PN-MES) state transition is a key process underlying malignant progression and therapeutic resistance. The present study was designed to elucidate the association between the PN-MES transition and arachidonic acid (AA) metabolic reprogramming in GBM. Methods: We integrated four public single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts, two spatial transcriptomic cohorts, and three bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts for GBM. By combinin
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data from multiple glioblastoma cohorts to link arachidonic acid metabolic reprogramming with the proneural-to-mesenchymal (PN-MES) state transition, a key driver of malignancy and therapy resistance. The findings suggest that AA metabolism is associated with the PN-MES transition, potentially offering new insights into GBM progression and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures. The authors found that these signatures are associated with prognosis and immune landscape, suggesting lactylation plays a role in tumor progression and immunity. The findings provide potential biomarkers for predicting outcomes and guiding immunotherapy in cervical cancer.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes the role of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), finding that EMCN expression is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and may serve as a potential prognostic biomarker. The authors provide evidence linking EMCN to immune infiltration and clinical outcomes in LUAD, filling a gap in knowledge about this gene's role in this cancer type.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma: single-cell and immune infiltration analyses.
papers.abstract: Zinc Finger Protein 695 (ZNF695) has been reported as a prognostic indicator in several cancers; however, its clinical implications and functional contributions within uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) have not yet been elucidated. Herein, the prognostic significance of ZNF695 in UCEC and its potential involvement in immune infiltration were examined.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC), finding that its expression is associated with patient prognosis and immune infiltration. Using single-cell and immune infiltration analyses, the authors suggest ZNF695 may serve as a prognostic biomarker and play a role in the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis, revealing common molecular pathways that may underlie both conditions. The findings provide potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for patients with APS at risk of CAS.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial landscape reveals impaired tertiary lymphoid structure maturation in Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are key immune niches involved in antitumor immunity. However, their functional impact depends on spatial localization, maturation status, and cellular composition within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Despite the recognized role of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) in gastric carcinogenesis and immune modulation, its influence on TLS architecture and function in gastric cancer remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study maps tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in gastric cancer using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, revealing that Helicobacter pylori infection impairs TLS maturation and alters their cellular composition within the tumor immune microenvironment. The findings suggest that H. pylori-driven disruption of TLS maturation may contribute to immune evasion in gastric cancer.

papers.title: FN1-associated cavernous endothelial remodeling induced by bisphenol A: relevance to erectile dysfunction and attenuation by baicalin.
papers.abstract: Previous studies suggest that bisphenol A (BPA) exposure may impair erectile function, but the underlying cavernous endothelial mechanisms remain unclear. Whether BPA induces endothelial alterations resembling those in diabetic erectile dysfunction (DMED) is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates how bisphenol A (BPA) exposure affects cavernous endothelial remodeling and erectile function, finding that BPA induces FN1-associated changes similar to those seen in diabetic erectile dysfunction. The authors also demonstrate that baicalin can attenuate these effects, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach.

papers.title: Disease-specific biomarker value of C-reactive protein and its composite indices in autoinflammatory diseases: an integrated study of multi-modal omics and population cohorts.
papers.abstract: Autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) are a heterogeneous group of innate immune-driven disorders whose prevalence is rising globally, yet the lack of disease-specific biomarkers continues to hamper accurate disease activity assessment, phenotype stratification, and risk evaluation. C-reactive protein (CRP) is one of the most widely used markers of systemic inflammation, yet its disease-specific expression, clinical correlations, network connectivity, and cellular origin across both adult and pediatric AIDs have not been systematically examined.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates C-reactive protein (CRP) and its composite indices as disease-specific biomarkers across multiple autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs), integrating multi-modal omics data with population cohorts. The findings reveal disease-specific CRP expression patterns, clinical correlations, and cellular origins, providing a foundation for improved disease activity assessment and phenotype stratification in both adult and pediatric AIDs.

papers.title: TPI1 promotes malignant progression and ferroptosis resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Triosephosphate isomerase 1 (TPI1) is aberrantly overexpressed and exerts a critical oncogenic role in the development and progression of various human cancers by regulating multiple malignant biological phenotypes. However, the biological functions of TPI1 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its regulatory effect on ferroptosis sensitivity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remain not fully elucidated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of TPI1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), finding that TPI1 is overexpressed and promotes malignant progression while conferring resistance to ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death. The findings suggest TPI1 as a potential therapeutic target in HNSCC.

papers.title: Neuronal precursor cell persistence in ganglioglioma is associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and immune cell infiltration.
papers.abstract: Gangliogliomas (GGs) are low-grade glioneuronal tumors that frequently present with drug-resistant epilepsy. Although their indolent course contrasts with their high epileptogenic potential, the oncogenic mechanisms sustaining neuronal precursor-like populations within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates gangliogliomas, low-grade brain tumors often associated with epilepsy, focusing on the tumor microenvironment. The findings reveal that persistent neuronal precursor-like cells in these tumors are linked to extracellular matrix remodeling and increased immune cell infiltration, providing new insights into the oncogenic mechanisms that sustain these cell populations.

papers.title: Aging-associated immune and stromal programs mark interferon- and remodeling-linked spatial contexts in psoriatic skin.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease characterized by spatially organized epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune interactions. Although aging is associated with inflammatory activation and tissue remodeling in skin, it remains unclear how aging-associated transcriptional programs are positioned within psoriatic tissue architecture and whether stromal cells with senescence-associated features retain inflammatory responsiveness.
papers.summary: This study maps aging-associated immune and stromal transcriptional programs within the spatial architecture of psoriatic skin, revealing that these programs are enriched in specific tissue contexts linked to interferon signaling and tissue remodeling. The findings suggest that senescent-like stromal cells in psoriatic lesions retain inflammatory responsiveness, potentially contributing to age-related differences in disease severity.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics and histopathological analyses reveal potential biomarkers and immune features linked to recurrence in head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck cancers (HNCs) are aggressive malignancies, with recurrence contributing substantially to poor patient outcomes. We used spatial transcriptomics to identify tumour and immune features associated with recurrence.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics combined with histopathological analysis to identify tumor and immune features associated with recurrence in head and neck cancers. The findings reveal potential biomarkers and immune-related characteristics that could help predict recurrence and guide treatment.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals the POSTN+ CAF-APOE+ macrophage axis drives immunosuppression and progression in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The progression of prostate cancer to lethal castration-resistant (CRPC) and metastatic (mCRPC) stages is driven by a profoundly remodeled tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the identity of key stromal cell populations, their developmental dynamics, and their precise crosstalk with immune cells remain incompletely understood, limiting our ability to target the TME therapeutically.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics analysis to identify a specific cellular axis in prostate cancer, involving POSTN+ cancer-associated fibroblasts and APOE+ macrophages, that promotes immunosuppression and tumor progression. The findings reveal a novel stromal-immune crosstalk mechanism that could be targeted therapeutically to overcome resistance in advanced prostate cancer.
